task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on REQ-162's design at lib/letflow/design/req162-lua-script-error-capture.md. CODE-DESIGNER's central claim: the consumed-instruction count IS reachable on the uncaught-error path, but via a DIFFERENT accessor than REQ-148's spike found for the success path -- the spike found `lua_after.state.instruction_count` after a successful eval; this design claims Lua.RuntimeException's own top-level :state field is always nil, but the WRAPPED exception in .original (Lua.VM.RuntimeError/TypeError/AssertionError) carries its own :state field with instruction_count, populated at every raise site in deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/executor.ex including the divide-by-zero and mod-by-zero sites. Independently re-verify this claim against the real vendored source -- do not trust the design doc's own account. Also verify the SCRIPT_ERROR-vs-4-other-arms distinguishability, the capability-state-at-failure wiring (and the honestly-disclosed gap that Sandbox.new/1 currently always installs an empty grant set), the 1//0 division substitution, and the stack-trace sanitization mechanism (SECURITY-REVIEWER will separately hard-gate this, but CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must confirm the design is coherent and complete first).
acceptance_criteria: Independently read deps/lua/lib/lua/runtime_exception.ex and deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/runtime_error.ex/type_error.ex/assertion_error.ex directly, and confirm Lua.RuntimeException's top-level :state field is genuinely always nil across every exception/1 clause, while the wrapped .original exception struct genuinely carries its own populated :state field with instruction_count -- do not take the design's citation at face value.
Confirm the divide-by-zero (1//0) and mod-by-zero (1%0) raise sites in deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/executor.ex genuinely pass state: state when constructing their error structs -- read the exact lines cited.

Confirm 1/0 genuinely yields inf (does not raise) and 1//0 genuinely raises 'attempt to divide by zero' in the real Lua 5.3 semantics this runtime implements -- verify against the vendored source's arithmetic implementation, not just the design's assertion.

Confirm the SCRIPT_ERROR shape is genuinely pattern-match-distinguishable from all 4 other real arms (SCRIPT_FAILED, instruction-budget, wall-clock timeout, memory-limit) by reading each of those 4 shapes directly in executor.ex.

Confirm the capability-state-at-failure field genuinely reads from REQ-157's real Capabilities type, and that the disclosed gap (Sandbox.new/1 currently always installs an empty grant set) is accurately described, not overstated or hidden.
Confirm the stack-trace sanitization design (using Lua.RuntimeException.to_map/2's Lua-level call_stack, never Elixir's __STACKTRACE__) is coherent and does not leave an obvious leak path.
All 8 real acceptance criteria in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-162 entry mapped to concrete design elements in a traceability table.
Zero literal Elixir code anywhere in the design doc -- @spec/@type only.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.
